newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria FinMin says to sell bank stake "soon".
newsitem.headline: Austria FinMin says to sell bank stake "soon".

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger said on Friday the state's 19 percent stake in market leader Bank Austria would be sold as soon as possible.
"The stake will, in accordance with the law, be sold as soon as possible," Edlinger said in a statement. Shares would be widely distributed.
Edlinger has previously insisted the state's stake in the bank would be sold before the end of the year and said that a placement on the Vienna stock exchange was just one of several options.
The shares have already been placed in the state-owned postal holding company in return for four to five billion schillings in cash in preparation for the sell-off.
Bank Austria in January bought the state's 70 percent voting stake in competitor Creditanstalt, creating Europe's 30th biggest banking group with some 13 billion schillings in combined assets.

According to a political agreement governing the sale, the state has to withdraw fully from the bank. The agreement also requires the City of Vienna, which wields effective control over Bank Austria through its AVZ foundation, to wind down its holding over the next five years.
The Austrian government also plans to partially privatise postal savings bank PSK, possibly before the end of the year.
Edlinger said PSK would be turned into a joint stock company and 49 percent of the shares sold off "as soon as possible". -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 274
